_comment: Starting-point profiles (degC). Times are for the stated reference weight at the base pit temperature, unwrapped unless noted. They are deliberately editable and will be re-fitted from the cook log. curve = planned probe temperature against fraction of cook time (0 = meat on, 1 = pull).

thigh.name: Thigh (bone-in, skin-on)
thigh.notes: Thighs eat best at 80-85C as the collagen renders. Weight barely changes time: pieces cook in parallel.

thigh_fillet.name: Thigh fillet (boneless)
thigh_fillet.notes: Boneless fillets cook faster than bone-in thighs. Probe the thickest fillet; take it to 80-85C for tender, rendered meat (safe from 74C). Lay them flat so thickness is even.

thigh_fillet_quick.name: Thigh fillet - quick (hot & fast)
thigh_fillet_quick.notes: Weeknight hot-and-fast, after GMG's Everyday Dinner Chicken Thighs: 420F (215C), about 30 min, flip at 15, dark meat to 79-85C (175-185F), rest 5-10 min.

breast.name: Breast
breast.notes: Pull at 72C and rest; carryover must take it to 74C or more (food-safety guideline).

spatchcock_recipe.name: Spatchcock herb-butter · recipe
spatchcock_recipe.pellets: Apple, fruitwood or GMG Gold Blend
spatchcock_recipe.prep: Cut out the backbone with poultry shears and flatten the breastbone. Pat dry. Rub: 20 g kosher salt, 10 g coarse pepper, 5 g garlic powder, 5 g smoked paprika; 40 g soft butter under the breast skin.
spatchcock_recipe.rest_note: Rest loosely tented with foil, then carve along the joints.
spatchcock_recipe.notes: Pull when the breast reads 74C and the thigh 80C (probe 2). Skin-side up the whole cook - never flip.

stages.name: Smoke infusion
stages.enter: Skin-side up on the centre grate. Probe 1 in the thickest breast, probe 2 in the thigh.

stages.name: Crisp & render
stages.enter: Pit up to 190C to render the skin. Don't flip.

prompts.text: Brush lightly with melted butter or glaze.

smoked_seared_thighs.name: Smoked & seared bone-in thighs · recipe
smoked_seared_thighs.prep: Trim excess skin and fat pockets. Coat with 15 ml olive oil and 25 g poultry rub.
smoked_seared_thighs.rest_note: Rest uncovered so the skin stays crisp.
smoked_seared_thighs.notes: Pull at 80C (78-82C range). The guide's table and quick-reference disagree on when to flip; this follows the table: render flip at ~55C, glaze from 70C.

stages.name: Smoke
stages.enter: Skin-side up (bone-side down) on the grates, probe in the thickest thigh away from the bone.

stages.name: Flip & render
stages.enter: Flip skin-side DOWN to render the fat; pit up to 175C.

stages.name: Glaze & set
stages.enter: Brush on the BBQ glaze and let it tack up.

point.name: Point end (deckle)
point.notes: Pull when probe-tender (probe slides in like butter), usually 93-98C.

flat.name: Flat
flat.notes: Leaner and thinner than the point: wrap a touch earlier to protect it from drying.

whole.name: Whole (packer)
whole.notes: Probe 1 in the thickest part of the flat (drives the plan), probe 2 in the point.

bone_in.name: Shoulder, bone-in
bone_in.notes: Ready to pull at 93-96C when the blade bone wiggles free.

pulled_pork_recipe.name: Pulled pork, Boston butt · recipe
pulled_pork_recipe.pellets: GMG Texas Blend (hickory, oak, mesquite) or apple
pulled_pork_recipe.prep: Score the fat cap in a 5 mm crosshatch. 30 ml yellow mustard as binder, then 50 g sweet & savoury pork rub. Best for 2.5-3.5 kg.
pulled_pork_recipe.rest_note: Wrap in an old towel and rest 1.5-2 h in an esky (keep it above 60C), then shred with the juices.
pulled_pork_recipe.notes: Pull at 95C or when the probe slides in with no resistance (95-98C).

stages.name: Bark formation
stages.enter: Fat cap UP, probe in the thickest part away from the bone.

prompts.text: Spritz with 50/50 apple juice and cider vinegar.

stages.name: Wrap (crutch)
stages.enter: Double-wrap tight in butcher paper or foil with 30 g brown sugar and 30 g butter, re-seat the probe. Pit up to 125C.

stages.name: Probe-tender test
stages.enter: Start probe-tender checks: it should slide in like warm butter.

spare_ribs_321.name: Spare ribs 3-2-1 · recipe
spare_ribs_321.prep: Peel the membrane off the back of the rack. Season both sides with 35 g pork rub.
spare_ribs_321.rest_note: Rest 10 min, then slice between the bones.
spare_ribs_321.notes: Timed cook - no probe needed. Done when the rack bends ~90 degrees without breaking (about 93-95C if you do probe).

stages.name: Smoke (3 h)
stages.enter: Bone-side down. Watch for the meat pulling back ~5 mm from the bone ends.

stages.name: Wrap (2 h)
stages.enter: Foil with 20 g butter, 15 ml honey, 15 ml apple juice; ribs meat-side DOWN; wrap tight. Pit to 115C.

stages.name: Glaze & set (1 h)
stages.enter: Unwrap, flip bone-side down and brush on the glaze. Pit to 110C.

prompts.text: Bend test: the rack should bend ~90 degrees without snapping.

rolled_roast_crackle.name: Rolled roast with crackling · recipe
rolled_roast_crackle.prep: Night before: score the skin, salt it and leave the roast uncovered in the fridge to dry. Season the inside, re-roll and tie every 2-3 cm so it's even end to end. Measure across the tied roll and enter it as Thickness - it sets the cook time better than weight.
rolled_roast_crackle.rest_note: Rest uncovered (foil softens the crackling), cut the string and slice 1 cm thick.
rolled_roast_crackle.notes: Sliced roast pork, pulled at 88-90C. Rolled meat carries the outside surface into the centre, so the centre must reach at least 75C.

stages.name: Smoke
stages.enter: Skin up, probe dead centre of the roll. Keep spritz and rub off the skin.

stages.name: Roast
stages.enter: Pit up to 160C to render the fat and soften the collagen.

stages.name: Crackle
stages.enter: Brush the skin with a little oil and salt. Pit to 250C to blister the crackling.

prompts.text: Check the crackling. Not puffing yet? Take the roast off and finish the skin under the oven grill for 3-5 min.

rolled_pulled.name: Rolled shoulder, pulled · recipe
rolled_pulled.pellets: Apple, cherry or GMG Texas Blend
rolled_pulled.prep: Take the skin off (keep it for crackling). Rub all over, including the inside, re-roll and tie every 2-3 cm. Measure across the tied roll and enter it as Thickness - it sets the cook time better than weight.
rolled_pulled.rest_note: Wrap in a towel and rest 1 h in an esky (keep it above 60C), then pull and mix through the juices. Optional: crisp the salted skin on the grill at 250C for 25-30 min while it rests.
rolled_pulled.notes: Pull at 95-96C when probe-tender. Start early if you can: the esky holds it hot for 2-3 h.

stages.name: Bark
stages.enter: Probe dead centre of the roll.

prompts.text: Spritz with 50/50 apple juice and cider vinegar.

stages.name: Wrap
stages.enter: Wrap tight in butcher paper or foil with a splash of apple juice, re-seat the probe. Pit to 125C.

stages.name: Probe-tender check
stages.enter: Start probe-tender checks: it should slide in like warm butter.

bone_in.name: Shoulder, bone-in
bone_in.notes: Wrap in foil with a splash of stock at ~70C; pulls apart at 90-93C.

lamb_rack_reverse_sear.name: Rack, reverse-seared · recipe
lamb_rack_reverse_sear.prep: Frenched rack (~800 g). Paste of 3 minced garlic cloves, 10 g chopped rosemary, 15 ml olive oil, 8 g sea salt, 5 g cracked pepper.
lamb_rack_reverse_sear.rest_note: Rest 8-10 min (it climbs to 57-58C), then slice between the bones.
lamb_rack_reverse_sear.notes: Medium-rare: pull at 55C. The rack comes OFF while the grill climbs to sear heat, so carryover doesn't overshoot.

stages.name: Gentle smoke
stages.enter: Bone-side down, probe in the centre of the eye.

stages.name: Heat for sear
stages.enter: Take the rack off and tent it with foil while the grill climbs to 260C.

stages.name: High-heat sear
stages.enter: Rack back on: flip every 90 seconds to build an even crust.

pulled_lamb_shoulder.name: 8-hour pulled shoulder · recipe
pulled_lamb_shoulder.prep: Season hard with sea salt, ground cumin, coriander seed, garlic powder and dried oregano. Best for 1.8-2.5 kg.
pulled_lamb_shoulder.rest_note: Rest 60 min in an esky or warm oven, then shred and toss through the reduced pan juices.

stages.name: Open smoke
stages.enter: Fat side up.

prompts.text: Spritz with 50/50 red wine vinegar and water.

stages.name: Pan braise
stages.enter: Into a foil tray with 150 ml beef stock and 2 rosemary sprigs, cover tightly. Pit up to 130C.

smoked_sausages.name: Slow-smoked snags & brats · recipe
smoked_sausages.prep: Don't prick the casings. Brush lightly with olive oil.
smoked_sausages.notes: Pull at 74C, safe for pork (72C) and chicken sausages (74C). The snap-crisp heat goes on at 68C because the pit takes ~10 min to climb to 190C.

stages.name: Low smoke
stages.enter: 2 cm apart on the upper rack, probe end-on into the thickest sausage.

stages.name: Flip & colour
stages.enter: Flip the sausages 180 degrees for even colour. Pit to 120C.

stages.name: Snap crisp
stages.enter: Pit to 190C to tighten the casings - pull the moment they hit 74C.

hasselback_potatoes.name: Hasselback potatoes · recipe
hasselback_potatoes.prep: 4 large Sebago or Russet potatoes (~250 g each), sliced every 3 mm stopping 5 mm from the base, garlic slivers in the cuts, 40 g melted butter and salt.
hasselback_potatoes.notes: Done at ~96C inside, when a skewer slides through with no resistance.

stages.name: Smoke & open
stages.enter: Straight onto the grates, probe in the centre of the largest potato.

prompts.text: Brush with the melted herb butter.

stages.name: Crisp exterior
stages.enter: Pit to 185C. Brush with bacon lard or clarified butter.

prompts.text: Flaky salt and Parmesan on now (optional).

balsamic_veg.name: Balsamic veg medley · recipe
balsamic_veg.prep: 500 g Kent pumpkin in 2 cm wedges, 2 zucchini in 2 cm rounds, 2 capsicums in 3 cm strips, 1 red onion in wedges. Toss with 30 ml olive oil, 5 g salt, 2 g pepper.
balsamic_veg.notes: Timed cook - no probe. The roast timer waits for the pit to reach 190C.

stages.name: Smoke infusion
stages.enter: Single layer on a perforated tray or wire rack.

stages.name: Roast & flip
stages.enter: Pit to 190C - the roast timer starts once it's up to heat.

stages.name: Glaze finish
stages.enter: Drizzle 30 ml balsamic reduction over the vegetables.
